book: Chapter 1, § 4, Exercise 15 (content/14-derived-algebra.typ, Exercise 1.4.15 `exc:codimension-one-normal-complement`): the counterexample to the printed statement without “normal”. In the group G of the maps x ↦ ax + b, a > 0 (the matrices [[a, b], [0, 1]] in GL(2, ℝ)), the subgroup H of the maps x ↦ ax is commutative and not normal: for g: x ↦ x + 1, h: x ↦ 2x, g h g⁻¹ = [[2, -1], [0, 1]] ∉ H.
limitations: Only the group-theoretic counterexample. Not formalized: that G is a connected solvable Lie group of dimension 2 and H a connected Lie subgroup of codimension 1 (evident from a = e^s), and the corrected statement with H normal.

book: Chapter 2, § 3, Problem 9 (with the added hypothesis char K = 0) and Hint 9 (content/23-dimension.typ, Problem 2.3.9 `pr:derivation-extends-algebraically` and its hint): the chain rule ∂(f(u)) = f^∂(u) + f'(u)∂u for a derivation (formula (2.3.1) with φ = id) and f ∈ A[T]; the linear equation f'(u)∂u + f^∂(u) = 0 for a root u; uniqueness of the extension to A[u] when f'(u) acts injectively; f'(u) ≠ 0 for the minimal polynomial over a field of characteristic 0; in characteristic p: derivations kill p-th powers, (X^p - t)' = 0, and d/dt on K[t] ⊂ K[s], t = s^p, extends to no derivation K[s] → L for any nontrivial K[s]-algebra L.
limitations: Derivations are additive maps with the Leibniz rule (K-linearity unused). Not formalized: the existence of the extension in characteristic 0 (construction and well-definedness on A[u]), the reductions to B = A[u] and to the field of fractions (Problem 8), the irreducibility of X^p - t over K(t), Problem 10 and Theorem 3.

book: Chapter 3, § 3, subsection “Engel's Theorem”, Problem 12 and Hint 12 (content/33-tangent-algebra.typ, Problem 3.3.12 `pr:unipotent-algebra-adjoint-unipotent` and its hint): commuting a, b with a^m = b^m = 0 give (a - b)^(2m-1) = 0; hence X^m = 0 gives (ad X)^(2m-1) = 0 on 𝔤𝔩(V) (any associative algebra over a commutative ring) and on every linear Lie algebra 𝔤 ⊂ 𝔤𝔩(V); so ad 𝔤 is unipotent if 𝔤 is.
limitations: Exactly the bound of Hint 12 and Problem 12; Engel's theorem (Theorem 6) and its corollaries are not formalized; sharpness of 2m - 1 is not checked.

book: Chapter 4, § 1, Hint 41 in the repaired reading (content/41-preliminaries.typ, the hint to Problem 4.1.41 `pr:root-vector-nonzero-on-string`): with [e_α, e_(-α)] = h_α, [h_α, e_α] = 2e_α and v ∈ V_μ, μ = λ - pα, h_α v = μ(h_α)v, e_(-α)v = 0: h_α e_α^k v = (μ(h_α) + 2k) e_α^k v and e_(-α) e_α^(k+1) v = -(k+1)(μ(h_α) + k) e_α^k v; U = span of e_α^k V_μ, 0 ≤ k ≤ s, is invariant under e_α, e_(-α), h_α when e_α^(s+1) V_μ = 0; e_α^k w ≠ 0 for k ≤ s if e_α^s w ≠ 0; the weights μ(h_α) + 2k (0 ≤ k ≤ s) are symmetric iff μ(h_α) = -s, so with μ(h_α) = -(p + q) they are not symmetric for s < p + q.
limitations: Any Lie module over a commutative ring; the relation [h_α, e_(-α)] = -2e_(-α) is not needed. Not formalized: Problem 40 (μ(h_α) = -(p + q) and integrality of weights), directness of the sum, the equality of the weight system of U with {μ(h_α) + 2k} as sets, and the Corollary of Theorem 5 that concludes Problem 41.

book: Chapter 4, § 2, subsection “Principal Definitions and Examples”, Problem 8 and its table (content/42-root-systems.typ, Problem 4.2.8 `pr:root-angles-and-length-ratios`), with ⟨λ|μ⟩ = 2(λ, μ)/(μ, μ): ⟨α|β⟩⟨β|α⟩ = 4cos²θ for nonzero α, β in a real inner product space; for non-proportional α, β with integer ⟨α|β⟩, ⟨β|α⟩ the product is 0, 1, 2 or 3; if both are nonpositive integers and |β| ≥ |α| then (⟨α|β⟩, ⟨β|α⟩, cos θ, |β|²/|α|²) is one of the six printed rows (cos θ = 0, -1/2, -√2/2, -√3/2, -1, -1).
limitations: θ enters through cos θ = (α, β)/(|α||β|); the angles π/2, 2π/3, 3π/4, 5π/6, π of the printed column follow from the standard cosine values and the injectivity of cos on [0, π], which are not rechecked here. The problem does not claim that every row occurs, and this is not checked.

book: Chapter 5, § 2, subsection “Lie Groups with Compact Tangent Algebras”, proof of Lemma 2 (content/52-compact-reductive.typ, Lemma 5.2.2 `lem:vector-group-finite-extension-splits`, formulas (5.2.4)–(5.2.8) `eq:splitting-homomorphism-ansatz`, `eq:factor-set-definition`, `eq:factor-set-coboundary-multiplicative`, `eq:conjugation-action-on-vector-group`, `eq:factor-set-coboundary-additive`, Problems 5.2.13 `pr:factor-set-cocycle-identity` and 5.2.14 `pr:cocycle-coboundary-by-averaging`): with f defined by (5), φ(x) = h(x)ψ(x) is multiplicative iff (6), in any group; the multiplicative form of Problem 13 (associativity); Problem 14: for a finite group L₀, a representation R₀ on a vector space A over a field of characteristic 0 and f satisfying Problem 13, h(x) = -(1/|L₀|) Σ_y f(x, y) satisfies (8).
limitations: The translation from the multiplicative identities to the additive ones (A commutative, f and h with values in A, conjugation by ψ(x) as the linear representation R₀, Problem 1.2.26) is not formalized; nor is the topological part of Lemma 2.

book: Chapter 6, subsection “Levi's Theorem”, Problems 5 and 6 as corrected and the paragraph after Problem 6 (content/60-levi-decomposition.typ, Problems 6.1.5 `pr:operators-scalar-on-radical` and 6.1.6 `pr:operators-scalar-on-radical-invariant`): for an ideal I (rad 𝔤) of a Lie algebra over a field, P = {v : v(𝔤) ⊂ I, v|I scalar} and Q = {v ∈ P : v|I = 0} are subspaces, Q ⊂ P, dim P - dim Q = 1 for finite-dimensional 𝔤 and I ≠ 0; with ρ(x)v = [ad x, v]: ρ(x)P ⊂ Q for every x ∈ 𝔤, P, Q, R = ad I are ρ(𝔤)-invariant; for commutative I and x ∈ I, ρ(x)v = ad(-cx) ∈ R; for x ∈ I, ad x ∈ P iff ad x ∈ Q iff [x, I] = 0, hence R ⊂ Q (and R ⊂ P) iff I is commutative; v₀ ∈ P with v₀|I = λE, λ ≠ 0 and ρ(𝔤)v₀ ⊂ R gives the projection v₀/λ onto I normalizing ad 𝔤.
limitations: Solvability of I is never used. Not formalized: the representation of 𝔤/rad 𝔤 in P/R, its complete reducibility (Corollary 3 of Theorem 5.2.13) and hence the existence of v₀, Problems 3 and 4, and the rest of the proof of Levi's theorem.
